title: Kung Pao Chicken
subtitle: Sichuan stir-fried chicken with chillies and peanuts
excerpt: Kung Pao chicken is a classic Sichuan stir-fry of tender chicken pieces tossed with dried chillies, peanuts, and a sweet-sour-spicy sauce. It is quick to cook and bold in flavour. Named after a Qing dynasty official, it is one of China's most famous dishes.
sourceNotes: Kung Pao chicken (Gong Bao Ji Ding) originates from Sichuan province and is named after Ding Baozhen, a Qing dynasty official whose title was Gong Bao. The dish combines dried chillies, peanuts, and a sweet-sour-spicy sauce. It was briefly banned in China during the Cultural Revolution but was later rehabilitated.

content.text: Kung Pao chicken is fast, fiery, and deeply satisfying. The key is high heat and having everything ready before the wok goes on. Once you start cooking, it moves quickly. Prep the sauce, marinate the chicken, and chop everything before you turn on the hob.

items.prepNote: use 50g roasted peanuts -- add at the end
or 6 dried whole chillies if available
mix with 2 tbsp water for the sauce thickener

content.text: Mix the soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, sugar, and 1 tablespoon of the cornflour-water mix in a small bowl. Set aside as the sauce.
Toss the chicken in 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and 1 teaspoon of the cornflour mix. Leave for 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok or wide frying pan over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken in batches until golden -- about 3 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil. Fry the chilli flakes for 30 seconds. Add the garlic, ginger, pepper, and spring onion. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pan. Pour over the sauce. Toss everything together over high heat until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken -- about 1 minute.
Add the peanuts. Toss once more. Serve immediately with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Sauce too sweet or too thin
items.cause: Sauce not reduced enough or ratio off
items.fix: Once the sauce goes in, keep the heat high and toss constantly. It should coat everything within 60 to 90 seconds. If too thin, mix a little more cornflour with cold water and add.

content.text: Kung Pao chicken is one of China's most famous dishes. It comes from Sichuan, a province known for bold, fiery flavours. The combination of numbing Sichuan peppercorns (optional here), dried chillies, and peanuts is distinctive. The dish is found across China and in Chinese restaurants around the world.
